summary: Verify every engineering claim in the external feedback against the code and map the four target areas

card.area: impala-card — JavaCard applet (ImpalaApplet/SCP03/TransactionParser), Kotlin SDK, jcardsim interop harness, docs (apdu.md, README.md), and the bridge endpoints the card talks to (POST /card, /auth/card*)
card.summary: The applet dispatches 19 CLA-0x00 commands plus SCP03 (0x50/0x82 at CLA 0x80; PROVISION_PIN 0x70 / APPLET_UPDATE 0x71 only at CLA 0x84 after C-MAC unwrap). Identity is a 16-byte accountId that is allocated all-zero in the constructor and never written by any command — INS_SET_CARD_DATA is a dead constant — so SIGN_AUTH always signs the nil UUID and bridge card login cannot verify against a real account. Card-to-card money is fully on-card: SIGN_TRANSFER debits the EEPROM balance and returns [DER sig(72 slot)|pubkey(65)|8-byte zero DER placeholder(72 slot)]; VERIFY_TRANSFER credits the balance after verifying the transfer signature against the public key carried in the message itself, never checking pubKeySig, never requiring a PIN, and never binding key to sender. Replay protection is a single per-recipient strictly-increasing int32 lastReceiveCounter (gaps allowed), committed atomically with the credit; 0x6233 is applet-local and undocumented. The 60-byte signable has no domain tag/version/network/expiry. SCP03 keys default to GP test keys 0x40..0x4F, no flag records that, and the provisioning gate can be lifted over a default-key channel. `terminated` is never set. README.md is stale (lists 50/51/RSA, wrong SIGN_AUTH shape); apdu.md is accurate. Interop tests (jcardsim, `./gradlew :sdk:jvmTest`) drive nearly every dispatched APDU including install params and SCP03.

Interop pins the zero id (AppletInteropTest.kt:58,:212). C-DEC optional; no auth-failure counter.

'LUK' occurs only in README.md:6 and ImpalaApplet.java:120 ('zero signature placeholder used for online (non-LUK) transfers where no pubKeySig is needed'); never defined in the repo. Industry meaning is Limited Use Key (issuer-certified offline key), matching the unused pubKeySig slot. The applet nonetheless implements SIGN_TRANSFER (:812-877) and VERIFY_TRANSFER (:891-963) which debit/credit the on-card balance with no bridge involvement — offline card-to-card. facts.fact: Dispatched CLA-0x00 INS set (switch :390-524): 0x2C INITIALIZE, 0x19 UPDATE_USER_PIN, 0x18 VERIFY_PIN, 0x02 NOP, 0x04 GET_BALANCE, 0x16 GET_ACCOUNT_ID, 0x64 GET_VERSION, 0x25 SIGN_AUTH, 0x06 SIGN_TRANSFER, 0x14 VERIFY_TRANSFER, 0x24 GET_EC_PUB_KEY, 0x20 GET_FULL_NAME, 0x1F SET_FULL_NAME, 0x21 GET_GENDER, 0x22 SET_GENDER, 0x1E GET_USER_DATA, 0x2E IS_CARD_ALIVE. Declared-but-dead: 0x07, 0x23, 0x26, 0x2B, 0x2D → 0x6D00.

CLA 0x80 only accepts INS 0x50 INITIALIZE UPDATE and 0x82 EXTERNAL AUTHENTICATE (else 0x6D00). CLA 0x84: 0x82 goes to processExternalAuthenticate; every other INS is first scp03.unwrapCommand()'d, then 0x70/0x71 are handled, otherwise it falls through to the normal switch (so any app command can be sent secured; sendBytes wraps the response via wrapResponse :1123-1134).

Persistent (EEPROM) state: initialized, terminated (never set true), accountId[16] (all-zero, unwritable), cardId[16] (random at install AND regenerated at INITIALIZE), currency[4] (all-zero, unwritable; when zero the currency check :833-839 is skipped), myBalance[8] uint64 BE, lastReceiveCounter[4], cardECPrivateKey/cardECPublicKey (null until INITIALIZE), fullName[128]+fullNameLength, gender[16]+genderLength, masterPIN OwnerPIN(10 tries, len 8, default 1,4,1,1,7,2,9,8), userPIN OwnerPIN(5 tries, maxLen 5, default 1,1,1,1), howManyPINless (byte), provisioningEnforced, pinProvisioned, SCP03 staticENC/MAC/DEK + session AESKey objects, AESCMAC k1/k2/state.

Transient CLEAR_ON_RESET buffers: scratchpad[255], sigBuffer[72], signableBuffer[60], tempAmount[8], tempCounter[4], hashBuffer[32], hashable.hash[32]+contents[252]; SCP03: hostChallenge[8], cardChallenge[8], macChainValue[16], derivationData[32], tempBuffer[32], encCounter[16], channelState[3] (state, secLevel, securedCmd).

INITIALIZE (0x2C) semantics: requires !terminated; if !initialized: randomData.setSeed(host bytes), regenerate cardId (16 random), createECKeypair() (KeyPair.genKeyPair — card-internal entropy), initialized=true; else 0x6686. No PIN, no gate, irreversible; there is no reset/terminate/SUICIDE path. Because cardId changes here, bridge registration (card_id = dash-stripped cardId UUID) must happen after INITIALIZE.

GET_EC_PUB_KEY: if cardECPublicKey==null it sends 65 bytes of scratchpad WITHOUT zeroing — zeros after reset but stale bytes (e.g. accountId||cardId||name from a prior GET_USER_DATA in the same session) otherwise. Pre-INITIALIZE SIGN_* answers 0x6230 (signWithMyKey :1098-1100).

SIGN_AUTH: data 8..64 bytes else 0x6700; message = "IMPALA-AUTH:"(12) || accountId(16) || challenge; ECDSA-SHA256 DER returned raw (≤72 bytes). Golden-pinned on both sides: AppletInteropTest.kt:198-220 and impala-bridge/src/handlers/card_auth.rs:380-404; bridge constant CARD_AUTH_DOMAIN_PREFIX constants.rs:227, CARD_SIGNATURE_MAX_BYTES=72.

SIGN_TRANSFER request = 4-byte PIN digits (raw values 0-9, not ASCII) + 60-byte signable (Lc must be 64 else 0x6226). Checks in order: PIN-less eligibility (:734-745: PIN==0000, amount<=200, howManyPINless<4, else 0x6690) or userPIN.check (fail → 0x69C0+tries); sender==accountId (0x6231); recipient!=accountId (0x6232); currency match if card currency non-zero (0x6229); amount<=balance (0x6224); counter MSB clear (0x6A80). Then sign, makeHashable (SHA-256 over 252-byte raw record, result unused), atomic {balance -= amount; howManyPINless++ if pinless}.

SIGN_TRANSFER response = 209 bytes: [0..72) sigBuffer (DER sig, trailing bytes of the slot are stale sigBuffer contents, not zeroed) | [72..137) uncompressed pubkey 04||X||Y | [137..145) 30 06 02 01 00 02 01 00 | [145..209) whatever was in scratchpad (not zeroed). SDK parses exactly 209 (ImpalaSDK.kt:250-260); tests trim DER by length byte (AppletInteropTest.kt:553-554).

VERIFY_TRANSFER: P1=0x00 with exactly 60 bytes → copy to signableBuffer (0x6226 otherwise). P1=0x01 with exactly 209 bytes (0x6C02 otherwise): sig@CDATA (length = buffer[CDATA+1]+2, host-controlled; a value ≥0x80 yields a negative length → crypto/AIOOBE), pubkey@CDATA+72 loaded into tempPubKey, pubKeySig@CDATA+137 ignored; verify → 0x0023 on failure; sender!=me (0x6231); recipient==me (0x6232); counter rule (0x6233); atomic {balance += amount (overflow → 0x6A80); lastReceiveCounter = counter}; signableBuffer zeroed. Any other P1 silently returns 0x9000. No PIN, no provisioning gate, no initialized check.

Signable byte layout (60): [0..8) dateTime int64 | [8..24) sender UUID | [24..40) recipient UUID | [40..44) currency | [44..48) amount uint32 (zero-extended to 8 bytes by getAmount) | [48..56) phoneId int64 | [56..60) counter int32. Host builder for tests: AppletInteropTest.kt:526-541.

Receive counter accept rule: accept iff counter in 1..0x7FFFFFFF (signed positive) AND counter > lastReceiveCounter (unsigned compare); gaps allowed; equal/lower → 0x6233. Counter is per receiving card regardless of sender; max value 0x7FFFFFFF is terminal (no reset/read command). Because VERIFY_TRANSFER needs no auth and accepts any P-256 key, anyone with NFC access can set lastReceiveCounter to 0x7FFFFFFF with a self-signed amount-0 transfer to recipient=accountId (currently all zeros on every card).

Install parameter format (gp --params / -Papplet.installparams, build.xml:24-28,:120-121): JavaCard array [aidLen][aid][ciLen][ci][adLen][appletData]; appletData = 01 <flags> [ENC16 MAC16 DEK16 if flags&02] [masterPIN8 userPIN4 if flags&04]; flags&01 = FLAG_INSTALL_ENFORCE. Validated fully before any mutation; errors 0x6A80 (SW_WRONG_DATA) or 0x6691 fail install. Empty/absent appletData = defaults, no gate. SimulatorBibo(installParams=...) builds the envelope for tests (SimulatorBibo.kt:53-58).

PROVISION_PIN (0x70, CLA 0x84 only) payload [pinType 0x81|0x82][len][PIN digits]; master must be 8, user 4 (0x6700), user 0000 → 0x6691, unknown type → 0x6A86; user PIN sets pinProvisioned=true; master PIN does not. No prior PIN required. APPLET_UPDATE (0x71) payload [seq(2)][len(2)][data]; seq 0x0001 + len 48 rotates ENC/MAC/DEK in place with no key-version bump; any other seq returns 0x9000 doing nothing (:724).

INITIALIZE UPDATE response = 29 bytes: 10 zero diversification bytes | KEY_INFO 02 03 70 | cardChallenge(8) | cardCryptogram(8). SDK hard-rejects keyVersion != 0x02 (SCP03Channel.kt:85-91, SCP03Constants.kt:22). Session keys via AES-CMAC KDF (GP Amd D), C-MAC over chaining value||header(wire Lc)||payload, counter-ICV C-DEC/R-ENC, R-MAC over chain||data||SW. EXTERNAL AUTHENTICATE requires P1 & 0x01 (C-MAC) else 0x6985; MAC/cryptogram mismatch → reset + 0x6300; unwrapCommand MAC mismatch → reset + 0x6688 (collides with SW_ERROR_NULL_POINTER_EXCEPTION). No auth-failure velocity counter.

SW codes defined in Constants.java (mirrored in Constants.kt): 0x9000, 0x6D00, 0x0022, 0x0023, 0x6A86, 0x6C01, 0x6C02 (SET_BALANCE_FAILED == WRONG_TAIL_LENGTH), 0x69C0-0x69C9, 0x6985, 0x6982, 0x6700, 0x6224, 0x6226 (PARSING_RECIPIENT == WRONG_SIGNABLE_LENGTH), 0x6227, 0x6229, 0x6230, 0x6231, 0x6232, 0x6677, 0x6678, 0x6679, 0x6683, 0x6684, 0x6685, 0x6686 (PRNG_ALREADY_SEEDED == ALREADY_INITIALIZED), 0x6687, 0x6688, 0x6689, 0x6690, 0x6691, 0x6C03, 0x6C04, 0x6F00, 0x4469, 0x6F15, 0x0000, 0x0001, 0x6300. Applet-local only (ImpalaApplet.java:64-84): 0x6233 TRANSFER_COUNTER_INVALID (used), 0x6201/0x6302/0x6301 (declared, unused). Also emitted: ISO 0x6A80 SW_DATA_INVALID/SW_WRONG_DATA.

apdu.md SW table omits 0x6233 (counter invalid), 0x6A80 (negative counter / balance overflow / bad DER / bad install params) and the 0x6688 SCP03-MAC-failure collision; otherwise apdu.md matches the dispatch code and already records the SET_CARD_DATA gap (:86-94,:169-172) and the untagged-SIGN_TRANSFER rationale (:55-57). New-INS procedure :174-188: add to Constants.java + Constants.kt, dispatch case, SDK method, MockBIBO test, doc row; reserve 0x30-0x4F; never reuse an INS.

jcardsim harness (SimulatorBibo → CardSimulator, fresh card per instance, install AID 01020304050607080102, optional install params) drives: GET_BALANCE, GET_ACCOUNT_ID, GET_VERSION, SET/GET_FULL_NAME, SET/GET_GENDER, IS_CARD_ALIVE, VERIFY_PIN user+master, INITIALIZE, GET_EC_PUB_KEY, SIGN_TRANSFER (PIN + PIN-less budget), VERIFY_TRANSFER both phases incl. raw tail replay, SIGN_AUTH (golden bytes, 8/64 bounds), UPDATE_USER_PIN raw, install-param keys/PINs/enforce/malformed, SCP03 open (default + injected keys), sec-level without C-MAC refused, CLA 0x84 without session (0x6985), CLA 0x80 0x70/0x71 → 0x6D00, PROVISION_PIN user+master, secured GET_BALANCE/GET_FULL_NAME. Not exercised: APPLET_UPDATE key rotation (SDK sendAppletUpdate exists, ImpalaSDK.kt:542-556), currency mismatch, PIN blocking, secured SIGN_TRANSFER.

SDK exposes dead-INS wrappers that will always throw ImpalaInstructionNotSupportedException against the applet: setCardData (CLA 0x00 0x26), updateMasterPin (0x2B), getRSAPubKey (0x07), getNonce (0x23). verifyTransfer sends two APDUs P1=0/1 (:275-283); signTransfer expects exactly 209 bytes; getImpalaAppletVersion expects exactly 10 bytes; secure channel default level 0x33; PIN digits mapped to raw values (:437-444).

Card registration: POST /card (main.rs:596) requires a bearer-authenticated user whose account_id equals payload.account_id (require_owner); INSERT card(account_id, card_id, ec_pubkey, rsa_pubkey) — rsa_pubkey is NOT NULL + UNIQUE (migrations/008_create_card.sql:7,:12) and must be 100-2048 base64 chars (validate.rs:206-221). The applet has no RSA key (0x07 → 0x6D00); the Android demo sends the empty byte array as "" (NfcCardAuthHelper.kt:180, CardsFragment.kt:101-108) → 400. card.account_id FK to impala_account (017), unique active card_id (021:31-32). card_id must be 8-32 hex; Android sends dash-stripped cardId UUID (ImpalaCardReader.kt:24).

POST /auth/card looks up SELECT account_id, ec_pubkey FROM card WHERE card_id=$1 AND is_delete=FALSE, requires account_id to parse as a UUID (:284-291, else 401), decodes ec_pubkey hex (must be 65-byte 0x04 point, :206-208), and verifies ECDSA_P256_SHA256_ASN1 over prefix||uuid||challenge for each live challenge (≤5 outstanding, 60 s TTL, consumed atomically). Only a bad signature over a live challenge counts toward lockout.

CAP built with ant-javacard v26 against jc310b43 kit targeting JavaCard 3.0.5 (applet.version 0.3 for the package; GET_VERSION reports BuildConfig MAJOR 0 / MINOR 1 / rev 0 / hash 00000000 — BuildConfig.java is a static stub). Firmware update = gp --delete + --install (reinstall target :151), which wipes all applet state; APPLET_UPDATE is explicitly not CAP replacement (ImpalaApplet.java:698-701).

README claims 'does not support offline LUKs; only online transactions are supported' and documents Set/Get Ext Pubkey (50/51), RSA pubkey, Update Master PIN, Set Card Data, a 24-byte SIGN_AUTH input and 7-byte git hash — none of which match the applet. ARCHITECTURE.md:317-372 likewise claims an RSA key pair and lists SET_CARD_DATA as a provisioning command. apdu.md is the accurate reference (apdu.md:8-11).

existing_controls: SIGN_AUTH is domain-tagged ("IMPALA-AUTH:"||accountId||challenge), challenge length 8..64 enforced on card and bridge, golden byte tests on both sides (AppletInteropTest.kt:198-220, card_auth.rs:380-404) — an auth signature cannot be replayed as a transfer signature.

Bridge card login: challenges are random 32 bytes, ≤5 outstanding per card, 60 s TTL, consumed atomically exactly once; unknown card / no live challenge / bad signature all return the same 401; only real signature failures count toward (card, source) lockout; registered card requires an existing account (FK) and unique active card_id.
POST /card requires a bearer-authenticated owner of the target account, is rate-limited per account, and validates card_id/ec_pubkey formats; bridge verifier rejects compressed keys.

Receive replay guard: strictly-increasing per-card lastReceiveCounter, zero/negative rejected, counter advance committed in the same JCSystem transaction as the balance credit; buffered signable is consumed after a successful credit so a repeated P1=0x01 tail cannot re-verify.

Send side: user PIN (OwnerPIN, 5 tries) or bounded PIN-less budget (≤200 units, ≤4 consecutive) with the counter incremented atomically with the debit; all-zero user PIN rejected in every PIN-setting path (install, PROVISION_PIN, UPDATE_USER_PIN); UPDATE_USER_PIN requires a validated master PIN and exactly 4 digits.

SCP03: PROVISION_PIN / APPLET_UPDATE reachable only through CLA 0x84 after per-command C-MAC verification; C-MAC bit mandatory at EXTERNAL AUTHENTICATE; constant-time MAC/cryptogram compares; counter-ICV encryption; session torn down on any MAC failure and on deselect; SDK refuses cards whose key version is not 0x02.

Install parameters are fully validated (tag, unknown flag bits, exact length, zero user PIN) before any state is applied, so a malformed install fails cleanly; FLAG_INSTALL_ENFORCE gates SIGN_TRANSFER/SIGN_AUTH until a user PIN is provisioned.
EC keypair entropy is card-internal (KeyPair.genKeyPair); the host INITIALIZE seed only supplements RandomData; INITIALIZE is one-shot.
Balance arithmetic is byte-wise unsigned with overflow (0x6A80) and underflow (0x6224) checks; amounts are zero-extended 4-byte integers — no floats.
Interop tests run the real applet in jcardsim as an independent crypto oracle for SCP03 and ECDSA; apdu.md is derived from the dispatch code and explicitly lists dead INS constants.

gaps.title: No personalization command: accountId and currency can never be set, so card login and sender checks run against the nil UUID
gaps.detail: accountId is new byte[16] (ImpalaApplet.java:201) with no write path; INS_SET_CARD_DATA (0x26) is undispatched. SIGN_AUTH therefore signs 'IMPALA-AUTH:'||00×16||challenge, which the bridge (card_auth.rs:284-291, :47-53) can only verify for an account whose UUID is nil. SIGN_TRANSFER's sender==accountId check (:817-822) means a real sender UUID is rejected with 0x6231, and every card in the field shares recipient 00×16. The SDK's setCardData() and the README's Set Card Data (38) describe a command that does not exist. Reserved-but-unused SWs (0x6C01 SET_ACCOUNT_ID_FAILED, 0x6677/0x6678/0x6679 card-data signature/nonce/card-id) and CardNonce.java show the original design was an issuer-signed, nonce-bound personalization.
gaps.suggested_approach: Implement INS_SET_CARD_DATA (0x26, keep the declared number) as an SCP03-only command: dispatch it in the CLA 0x84 branch next to 0x70/0x71 (ImpalaApplet.java:377-386) so it inherits unwrapCommand's C-MAC requirement and is rejected at CLA 0x00 with 0x6D00 as today. Payload: accountId(16) || currency(4) [|| optional cardId(16) if the issuer must control card_id]; require the channel to have C-DEC (channelState secLevel & 0x02) so the UUID is not sent in clear; write both fields in one JCSystem transaction; make it write-once (accountId non-zero → 0x6C01) unless the ENFORCE policy allows re-personalization, and require !pinProvisioned-or-master-PIN as you prefer. Keep failIfCardIsTerminated. Order for a fresh card: install(params) → INITIALIZE → SET_CARD_DATA over SCP03 → GET_USER_DATA/GET_EC_PUB_KEY → POST /card. SDK: change setCardData() to build a typed payload and send via secureTx; add MockBIBO test + interop test that then asserts sdk.getAccountId() == the provisioned UUID and that a SIGN_AUTH verifies host-side over that UUID. Update apdu.md (remove from the dead list, add row + SW), Constants.kt unchanged. Compatibility: additive INS — already-flashed cards answer 0x6D00 and remain unusable for login exactly as now; SDK/Android/bridge parsers are untouched. Bridge side note: card auth accounts must have UUID account ids; consider a bridge check at POST /card that account_id parses as a UUID.

gaps.title: Bridge POST /card cannot be satisfied by this applet: rsa_pubkey is mandatory, validated 100-2048 base64 chars, and UNIQUE
gaps.detail: The applet has no RSA key (INS 0x07 → 0x6D00, createECKeypair only). validate_rsa_pubkey (validate.rs:206-221) rejects the Android demo's empty string (NfcCardAuthHelper.kt:180 → CardsFragment.kt:101) with 400, and migrations/008_create_card.sql:7,:12 make rsa_pubkey NOT NULL and UNIQUE, so even a shared placeholder could register only one card. The card-auth flow (card_auth.rs) never reads rsa_pubkey. This blocks end-to-end registration independently of the accountId gap.
gaps.suggested_approach: In impala-bridge: make CreateCardRequest.rsa_pubkey Option<String> (models.rs:512-517), validate only when Some, and add a migration that drops NOT NULL and replaces UNIQUE(rsa_pubkey) with a partial unique index WHERE rsa_pubkey IS NOT NULL (run the migration before rolling the binary — CLAUDE.md rule). Recount the INSERT bind sites (card.rs:43-54 is the only one). Update openapi.yaml and ARCHITECTURE.md (which claim an RSA key pair). Android: send null when getRSAPubKey fails. No applet or SDK change; existing rows unaffected.

gaps.title: VERIFY_TRANSFER accepts any P-256 key: unauthenticated on-card credit and a one-tap receive-counter jam DoS
gaps.detail: Phase 2 loads the pubkey from the message tail (:904) and verifies the transfer signature with it (:906-909); pubKeySig (bytes 137..208) is never read, no key-to-sender binding exists, no PIN/gate/initialized check applies, and the recipient id on every card is currently the nil UUID. Consequences: (1) anyone holding the card can inflate its balance with a self-generated keypair (the interop test does exactly this, AppletInteropTest.kt:93-104), so the on-card ledger proves nothing to a counterparty; (2) anyone with a second of NFC access can send a self-signed amount-0 transfer with counter 0x7FFFFFFF and permanently prevent the card from ever accepting a credit (no counter read/reset exists).
gaps.suggested_approach: Add an issuer (program) public key to the card and verify a certificate over the sender key before trusting it. Concretely: persistent `programPublicKey` (ECPublicKey via SecP256r1.newPubKey()) installed either by a new install-param flag 0x08 followed by 65 bytes (extend applyProvisioningParameters' expectedLength/offset logic) or by APPLET_UPDATE seq 0x0002 + len 65 (both already SCP03-protected); a persistent 72-byte `cardKeyCert` written by the same channel after INITIALIZE (the issuer signs SHA-256(accountId(16)||cardPubKey(65)) with the program key — this also binds the key to the sender UUID). SIGN_TRANSFER returns cardKeyCert in the third slot instead of SIXTY_FOUR_ZEROES (wire layout 72|65|72 unchanged, so ImpalaSDK.signTransfer and any parser keep working). VERIFY_TRANSFER phase 2: if programPublicKey.isInitialized(), verify pubKeySig over sender||pubkey with the `verifier` engine first (fail → 0x0022, already reserved) and only then verify the transfer signature; reject with 0x6230 if no program key is provisioned and ENFORCE is set. Additionally bound counter jumps (e.g. reject counter > lastReceiveCounter + 0x00100000 with 0x6233) so a compromised issuer key still cannot jam a card in one step, and add a read command for lastReceiveCounter (see next gap). Compatibility: senders flashed with the old CAP present a zero placeholder and will be rejected by new receivers (intended); since no fielded card can hold a real accountId today, there is no functional deployment to break. Interop test: generate a program key in the test, install it via params, mint the cert with JCA, assert the ad-hoc-key funding now fails with 0x0022 and the certified one succeeds.

gaps.title: SIGN_TRANSFER signable is untagged and unversioned: no protocol/network/type discriminator, no expiry, dateTime/phoneId unchecked
gaps.detail: The card signs the raw 60 bytes (:851); the same signature bytes are valid on testnet and live cards, for any future message type that happens to be 60 bytes, and forever (the card has no clock, and it never inspects dateTime/phoneId). The only reason given (:803-804, apdu.md:55-57) is compatibility with already-flashed CAPs — but those CAPs cannot hold an accountId, so nothing deployed depends on the current bytes.
gaps.suggested_approach: Prefix the signed message with a fixed tag and the applet's own instance AID, which differs per network with no new state: sign "IMPALA-XFER:"(12) || AID (JCSystem.getAID().getBytes into scratchpad, 10 bytes) || signable(60); VERIFY_TRANSFER rebuilds the same prefix from its own AID before verifying, so cross-network replay fails automatically. Reserve one byte of a version (e.g. 0x01) after the tag so the bridge can discriminate. Do it under new INS numbers in the reserved range (0x30 SIGN_TRANSFER_V2 / 0x31 VERIFY_TRANSFER_V2, same request/response byte layouts) rather than mutating 0x06/0x14, per apdu.md's never-reuse rule; keep 0x06/0x14 dispatching for one release and then remove them (→0x6D00). SDK: add signTransferV2/verifyTransferV2 (or a version switch keyed on getImpalaAppletVersion — bump BuildConfig MINOR when shipping). Expiry cannot be enforced on-card; document that the bridge/host must reject stale dateTime when it ingests transfers. Compatibility: additive INS, identical parsers; old CAPs interoperate with each other only via the old INS pair.

gaps.title: Receive counter is undocumented, unreadable, and 0x6233 is missing from Constants/SDK/apdu.md
gaps.detail: The allocation contract ('one strictly increasing int32 stream per recipient, host-allocated, gaps OK, max 0x7FFFFFFF') exists only as a code comment (:933-941); no host can read the current value to resync after a gap or a lost transfer; 0x6233 is declared only inside ImpalaApplet.java (:71) so Constants.java/Constants.kt lack it, ImpalaException.fromStatusWord maps it to a generic 'Unknown status word', and apdu.md's SW table omits it (also omits 0x6A80 and the 0x6688 SCP03/NPE collision).
gaps.suggested_approach: Add SW_ERROR_TRANSFER_COUNTER_INVALID=0x6233 to Constants.java and Constants.kt, a case in ImpalaException.fromStatusWord (ImpalaTransferException), rows in apdu.md's SW table for 0x6233 and 0x6A80, and a short 'Transfer counter' section documenting the accept rule and the host allocation/recovery procedure. Add a read command in the reserved range (e.g. 0x32 GET_RECEIVE_COUNTER → 4 bytes, no auth, mirrors GET_BALANCE) rather than widening GET_USER_DATA (its trailing bytes are parsed as fullName by both SDK ImpalaCardUser and Android CardUser). Give SCP03's MAC failure its own SW (e.g. 0x6982, already declared as SW_SECURITY_STATUS_NOT_SATISFIED) instead of 0x6688. Interop test: after a gap credit, assert the new command returns the last accepted counter. Compatibility: additive.

gaps.title: SCP03 default GP test keys are indistinguishable from real keys, and the provisioning gate can be lifted with public keys
gaps.detail: Keys default to 0x40..0x4F (:236-244); no persistent flag records that; KEY_INFO/diversification are constants so a host cannot tell key sets apart; nothing is gated on non-default keys. A card installed with FLAG_INSTALL_ENFORCE but without FLAG_INSTALL_KEYS can have PROVISION_PIN run by anyone who knows the published test keys, setting both PINs and lifting the SIGN gate; the same channel rotates keys via APPLET_UPDATE. C-DEC is optional, so a host choosing level 0x01/0x11 sends PIN digits in clear over NFC (SDK default 0x33 is fine). No EXTERNAL AUTHENTICATE failure counter exists.
gaps.suggested_approach: Add persistent boolean `scp03KeysDefault` (true in constructor; false when FLAG_INSTALL_KEYS applies or APPLET_UPDATE seq 0x0001 succeeds). When provisioningEnforced, refuse PROVISION_PIN, SET_CARD_DATA and program-key installation while scp03KeysDefault (0x6985), so an ENFORCE card must be keyed at install or immediately rotated by the issuer before anything else. Require SEC_CDEC on the session for PROVISION_PIN/SET_CARD_DATA (check channelState secLevel inside those handlers). Add a persistent SCP03 auth-failure counter (byte, e.g. block at 10, reset on success) in processExternalAuthenticate. Put the first 10 bytes of cardId into KEY_DIVERSIFICATION so hosts can derive per-card keys (standard GP; the SDK ignores those bytes today, SCP03Channel.kt:80-83). Do not change KEY_INFO[0] — the SDK pins 0x02. Compatibility: install-param wire format unchanged; test-key cards without ENFORCE keep working (jcardsim harness relies on defaults); add interop tests for the new refusals.

gaps.title: impala-card/README.md (and ARCHITECTURE.md's card section) are stale relative to the applet
gaps.detail: README:6 says offline LUKs are unsupported and only online transactions exist, while SIGN_TRANSFER/VERIFY_TRANSFER move on-card balance offline; 'LUK' (Limited Use Key) is never defined; README lists Set/Get Ext Pubkey (50/51) that exist nowhere, RSA key operations that do not exist, a 24-byte SIGN_AUTH input/36-byte output, a 7-byte git hash, and 'may only be invoked once' for INITIALIZE without the 0x6686 detail. ARCHITECTURE.md:317 claims an RSA key pair and :346 lists SET_CARD_DATA as a live provisioning command.
gaps.suggested_approach: Replace README's 'Supported APDUs' section with a pointer to docs/apdu.md, define LUK once (issuer-certified limited-use key enabling offline verification — the pubKeySig slot) and state plainly that transfers are offline card-to-card with off-card settlement; delete the 50/51/RSA entries; fix ARCHITECTURE.md's card-state table (add lastReceiveCounter, howManyPINless, provisioning flags, drop RSA) and the SET_CARD_DATA box until the command exists. Docs-only, no compatibility impact.

gaps.title: Dead lifecycle and hygiene issues: `terminated` never set, unzeroed response padding, stale-scratchpad pubkey pre-INITIALIZE, host-controlled DER length, duplicate SW values
gaps.detail: terminated is only ever assigned false (:199) and INS_SUICIDE is undispatched, so every failIfCardIsTerminated check is dead; SIGN_TRANSFER's 72-byte slots carry stale sigBuffer/scratchpad bytes after the DER (:872-876); GET_EC_PUB_KEY before INITIALIZE returns 65 uncleared scratchpad bytes (:464-470); verifyTransfer derives sigLength from buffer[CDATA+1] without bounds (:908) so a length byte ≥0x80 or >70 yields a negative/oversized length and an unmapped exception; SW aliases 0x6226/0x6C02/0x6686 are double-defined and 0x6201/0x6301/0x6302 are unused; VERIFY_TRANSFER with P1∉{0,1} returns 0x9000.
gaps.suggested_approach: Either implement termination as an SCP03-only command (new INS in 0x30 range that sets terminated=true, or APPLET_UPDATE seq 0x0003) or delete the flag and checks; zero-fill scratchpad[0..209) before assembling the SIGN_TRANSFER response and scratchpad[0..65) in the null-key branch; validate 8 ≤ buffer[CDATA+1]+2 ≤ 72 before verifySig (else 0x6A80); add a default branch in verifyTransfer (0x6A86); remove or rename the duplicate SW constants in both Constants files. All are compatible with existing parsers (slot sizes unchanged).

constraints: JavaCard 3.0.5 target (build.xml:57, jc310b43 converter, ant-javacard v26, JDK 17 for Gradle+Ant): no int arithmetic, short/byte arrays only, persistent allocations must happen in the constructor, APDU buffer assumed ≥261 bytes by SCP03.unwrapCommand/wrapResponse in-place MAC building.

Never reuse an INS number; new commands go in 0x30–0x4F; every new INS must be added to Constants.java AND Constants.kt, get a dispatch case, an ImpalaSDK method, a MockBIBO unit test in ImpalaSDKTest.kt, and a row in docs/apdu.md (apdu.md:174-188).

Wire layouts parsed by clients and pinned by tests must stay byte-compatible unless versioned: SIGN_TRANSFER response exactly 209 = 72|65|72 (ImpalaSDK.kt:250-260, ImpalaSDKTest.kt:162-174); GET_USER_DATA = accountId16|cardId16|fullName-rest (SDK ImpalaUser.kt:18-29, Android CardUser.fromCardData); GET_VERSION exactly 10 bytes; GET_EC_PUB_KEY 65-byte 0x04 point; SIGN_AUTH raw DER ≤72 bytes over "IMPALA-AUTH:"||uuid16||challenge(8..64) — golden tests on card (AppletInteropTest.kt:198-242) and bridge (card_auth.rs:380-404, constants.rs:227-242) must both pass.

SCP03 INITIALIZE UPDATE key-version byte must remain 0x02 (SDK hard-fails otherwise, SCP03Channel.kt:85-91); install-parameter TLV [0x01][flags]… is consumed by SimulatorBibo tests and gp --params; unknown flag bits are rejected, so new flags must be added to the mask at ImpalaApplet.java:610.
PIN digits travel as raw values 0..9 (not ASCII) everywhere; all-zero user PIN is reserved for PIN-less transfers and must stay rejected in every PIN-writing path.

Money invariants: balance/counter mutations stay inside a single JCSystem.beginTransaction/commitTransaction; unsigned byte-wise arithmetic with explicit overflow/underflow SWs; amounts are 4-byte zero-extended integers.

Firmware changes require gp delete+install (APPLET_UPDATE is not CAP replacement), which wipes all state; INITIALIZE is one-shot; SCP03 static keys and PINs are default unless install params or PROVISION_PIN/APPLET_UPDATE changed them — plan any reflash as a full re-provisioning.

Test harness: `cd impala-card && ./gradlew :sdk:jvmTest` (jcardsim 3.0.6.0, fresh CardSimulator per SimulatorBibo, no persistence across instances, JCA-backed ECDSA/AES); caprunner (`gradle caprunnerTest`) is non-blocking and cannot execute ECDSA; CI job `test` gates CAP builds (.github/workflows/impala-card.yml).

Bridge contract: card_id 8–32 lowercase hex (Android sends dash-stripped cardId UUID), ec_pubkey 130-hex uncompressed for auth, account ids used with cards must be RFC-4122 UUIDs; migrations are operator-run before binary roll; card table currently has NOT NULL UNIQUE rsa_pubkey.

On-card there is no clock and no issuer key today; any expiry or issuer-certification semantics must be added as explicit state/commands, and the bridge must remain the source of truth for settlement (on-card balance is advisory).

soroban.area: impala-soroban — MultisigUsdcWrapper contract (integration-test/src/lib.rs), testnet-tests, README, CI
soroban.summary: One 745-line Soroban contract (plus 55 inline unit tests, lines 747-1968) pinned to soroban-sdk 23.5.3 / soroban-env-host 23.0.1. `initialize` is an ordinary unauthenticated entry point guarded only by an `Initialized` instance key; the token is validated by `symbol()=="USDC"` and `decimals()==7` only (decimals is hardcoded 7 for every SAC, so that check is a no-op against SACs). Every key — config, WrappedUsdc {token, decimals, total_wrapped}, Balance(Address), TimeLock(u64), NextTimeLockId, MinLockDuration, Paused, Initialized — lives in instance storage with one shared TTL (extend when <120,960 ledgers left, to 518,400). Scheduling checks balance advisorily and reserves nothing; execute_* take only a timelock_id, re-run `verify_multisig` over the *stored* signer vector against the *current* config (every stored signer must `require_auth`, not just threshold), so rotation strands pending timelocks. cancel needs current multisig and works while paused. No reserved-balance, no execution window, no min-threshold invariant on rotation. Tests are example-based with `mock_all_auths` and direct storage seeding; only two tests spot-check conservation; no proptest/fuzz; CI (toolchain 1.96.0, wasm32-unknown-unknown) uploads the WASM as a 30-day artifact with no hash or manifest. The SAC's `name()` returns "CODE:ISSUER", which makes issuer pinning possible in-contract.

facts.fact: `initialize(env, signers: Vec<Address>, threshold: u32, usdc_token: Address, min_lock_duration: u64)` — no auth; order of checks: Initialized(153) → threshold(157) → len<=20(161) → duplicates(168) → min_lock<=MAX(171) → symbol(176-179) → decimals(180-183) → writes(185-204) → extend TTL(206).

DataKey variants: MultisigConfig, WrappedUsdc, Balance(Address), Initialized, TimeLock(u64), NextTimeLockId, MinLockDuration, Paused. Stored values: MultisigConfig{signers: Vec<Address>, threshold: u32} (:54-59); WrappedUsdc{usdc_token: Address, decimals: u32, total_wrapped: i128} (:63-70); Balance → i128 (absent = 0); TimeLock → TimeLock struct; NextTimeLockId → u64 starting at 0; MinLockDuration → u64; Paused → bool (absent = false); Initialized → true.

TimeLock{operation_type: u32 (1=unwrap, 2=transfer), signers: Vec<Address>, sender: Address, recipient: Address, amount: i128, unlock_time: u64 (ledger timestamp seconds), executed: bool}. For unwrap, sender==recipient (:369-370). Contract-type field additions change the XDR spec of get_timelock's return.
Constants: MAX_LOCK_DURATION=31_536_000 s (365 d); USDC_DECIMALS=7; MAX_SIGNERS=20; INSTANCE_TTL_THRESHOLD=7*17_280=120,960 ledgers; INSTANCE_TTL_EXTEND_TO=30*17_280=518,400 ledgers.

`extend_instance_ttl` = `env.storage().instance().extend_ttl(120_960, 518_400)`; invoked by initialize, bump_ttl (permissionless, no auth), pause, unpause, rotate_signers, wrap, schedule_unwrap, execute_unwrap, schedule_transfer, execute_transfer, cancel_timelock. Read-only fns (get_timelock, balance, total_supply, usdc_token, usdc_decimals) never extend.

`verify_multisig(env, provided)`: panics "Insufficient signers" if provided.len() < config.threshold; "Duplicate signer detected" via O(n²) require_no_duplicates; "Signer not authorized" if any provided address is not in config.signers; then `require_auth()` on EVERY provided signer (all of them, not a threshold subset). Config read is the current MultisigConfig.

`wrap(env, signers, depositor, amount)`: require_not_paused → amount>0 → verify_multisig → depositor.require_auth() → TTL → token.transfer(depositor→contract) → Balance(depositor)+=amount (checked_add, "Balance overflow") → total_wrapped+=amount ("Total supply overflow") → event ("wrap", depositor) = amount.

`schedule_unwrap(env, signers, recipient, amount, delay_seconds) -> u64`: gates paused, amount>0, multisig, delay>=MinLockDuration ("Delay too short"), delay<=MAX ("Delay exceeds maximum lock duration"), Balance(recipient)>=amount ("Insufficient wrapped balance", advisory); unlock_time = ledger.timestamp + delay (checked_add). The balance holder (recipient) does NOT require_auth — signers control all balances (custodial model). Event ("sched_unw", recipient, id) = unlock_time.

`schedule_transfer(env, signers, from, to, amount, delay_seconds) -> u64`: same gates plus from!=to ("Self-transfer not allowed"); Balance(from)>=amount ("Insufficient balance", advisory); `from` does not require_auth. Event ("sched_tx", from, to, id) = unlock_time.

`execute_unwrap(env, timelock_id)`: require_not_paused → get TimeLock ("Timelock not found") → executed? ("Already executed") → timestamp>=unlock_time ("Timelock not expired") → verify_multisig(stored signers) → TTL → Balance(recipient)>=amount ("Insufficient balance") → set executed=true → Balance-=amount → token.transfer(contract→recipient) → total_wrapped-=amount → remove TimeLock → event ("exec_unw", recipient, id)=amount. No signers parameter.

`execute_transfer(env, timelock_id)`: identical gates; Balance(sender)-=amount, Balance(recipient)+=amount (checked), remove TimeLock, event ("exec_tx", sender, recipient, id)=amount. No external call, no total_wrapped change.

`cancel_timelock(env, signers, timelock_id)`: verify_multisig(current config) → TTL → get ("Timelock not found") → executed? → remove → event ("cancel", id)=0. NOT gated by pause; no check that the canceller relates to the timelock; does not read timelock.sender/amount (relevant if reserved-balance accounting is added).

`rotate_signers(env, current_signers, new_signers, new_threshold)`: checks new non-empty, 1<=new_threshold<=new_len, new_len<=20, no duplicates, then verify_multisig(current). Overwrites MultisigConfig; pending TimeLocks keep their stored signer vectors and are re-verified against the NEW config at execute time. Event ("rotate",)=new_threshold. No lower bound on threshold, no delay/timelock on rotation.

pause/unpause require multisig and set Paused; require_not_paused (:687-696) gates wrap, schedule_unwrap, execute_unwrap, schedule_transfer, execute_transfer only. pause, unpause, rotate_signers, cancel_timelock, bump_ttl and all reads work while paused. A timelock that matures during a pause remains executable forever after unpause (no expiry window).

bridge.area: impala-bridge conservation controls on the custodial (/managed-account/sign) and conversion-reserve money paths
bridge.summary: The bridge models money in four unrelated ledgers with no cross-domain spec. (1) Custodial: managed_seed rows (KMS/Vault-envelope ciphertext, one per account) sign native-XLM payments in-process via POST /managed-account/sign; the ONLY controls are owner scoping, the reserve-account quarantine, and a 5/min Redis rate limit; the transaction row is inserted after settlement with no intent, no idempotency key, no amount, no limits, no pause. (2) Conversion reserve: Postgres buckets (available/held) plus an append-only journal, every mutation a guarded single-statement UPDATE + journal row in one tx, write-ahead intents (payout_attempt/refund_intent/replenish_attempt) before every submit, ambiguous submits freeze for a human, per-payment paging_token anchors make Horizon replay a no-op, caps/kill-switches exist for refunds/replenishment/quotes. (3) Payala: the "Payala backend" is external and never called; POST /sync/payala ingests client-asserted offline batches (idempotent per (account, payala_tx_id)) into payala_reserve (net) or mirror transaction rows, explicitly quarantined from on-chain value; the Payala TCP stream just dumps raw JSON into Redis. (4) Card: the int64 balance lives on the JavaCard and never reaches the bridge. The outbox is transactional by type (emit_event takes &mut Transaction) with three audit-after-commit exceptions and no event at all on the custodial sign path. Signing is in-process everywhere (seed decrypted into SecretBytes, ed25519 via stellar-base).

The bridge registers only card_id + EC/RSA pubkeys (models.rs:512-517) and verifies auth challenges (card_auth); no card balance or transfer amount is ever sent to or stored by the bridge.

impalactl already documents the hole: 'The bridge ... records the transaction row only AFTER settlement ... the bridge's own request deadline can fire mid-submission, which drops the bookkeeping while the payment still lands'; it tells users a re-run is a second payment and to check activity list then the chain (impalactl account onchain).

Tests on the sign module: test_require_owner_rejects_mismatch, test_validate_names, a_sealed_seed_round_trips_under_its_own_account, a_sealed_seed_does_not_open_under_another_account, a_binding_failure_never_echoes_seed_material, legacy_unbound_seeds_still_open, seed_and_credential_headers_are_distinct, the_reserve_quarantine_is_armed_without_a_live_reserve, no_reserve_configured_quarantines_nothing. None exercise duplicate requests, timeouts, or bookkeeping loss.

existing_controls: Custodial sign: owner scoping (require_owner), reserve-account quarantine keyed off configuration (ReserveAccountGuard, managed_seed.rs:49-61), per-account Redis rate limit 5/60s fail-closed, destination strkey validation, seed backend match + bound header + derived-address assertion (load_protected_seed), SecretBytes zeroize-on-drop, synchronous server-only signing (never SQS), TX_TIMEOUT_SECS=300 time bounds on every signed tx, Stellar sequence numbers (tx_bad_seq) stop only CONCURRENT duplicates.

Reserve ledger: guarded single-statement bucket UPDATEs (RESERVE_HOLD_SQL fraction guard <=50% held, RESERVE_BUCKET_APPLY_SQL non-negative), append-only journal with balance_after snapshots under row lock, UNIQUE(order_id,kind)/(quote_id,kind)/(cycle_id,kind) idempotency anchors, per-payment paging_token anchors, monotonic Horizon cursor advanced only after commit, write-ahead intents (payout_attempt, refund_intent, replenish_attempt) before every submit, definitive-vs-ambiguous submit classification with freeze-never-resubmit, stale sweeps at 600s, admin resolve that verifies chain state (min intent age 600s, Horizon lag <=90s) before releasing holds, per-account advisory locks, RESERVE_MAX_OPEN_ORDERS_PER_ACCOUNT=3, bounded payout/refund retries (5/3).

Reserve money policy: per-provider divert policy enabled+threshold ($20-$200), refunds master switch (conversion_reserve_state.refunds_enabled, re-read every tick), per-bucket refund_max_minor and refund_daily_max_minor (0 = disabled) with a 24h spend sum under the bucket lock, refund cooldown 300s (ops cancel window), replenish policy enabled/max_spend/daily_spend_cap/min_float/min_price/max_slippage with '0 = unconfigured -> refuse', one cycle in flight per kind (uq_crr_inflight), quote kill switch, low_water alerts, issuer burn-guards, trustline audit.

Payala sync: idempotent per (account, payala_tx_id), one tx per batch under an advisory lock, batch size/currency/overflow validation, conflicting-replay detection (counted), explicitly quarantined from on-chain value.
Outbox/webhooks: emit_event only inside a Transaction; delivery at-least-once with leases, guarded marks, ON CONFLICT fan-out, HMAC signatures, SSRF re-validation; money tables never pruned.

Key custody: envelope encryption (KMS/Vault/OpenBao), no plaintext at rest, seed material never returned/logged, install-only key endpoints with fingerprints, reserve seed generate-only, ManageKeys/ManageReserve capability gating with tripwire tests pinning handler extractors and migration CHECK lists.

Auth/infra fail-closed: bearer/session validation and rate limits fail closed on Redis outage (tests auth.rs:551,588), shutdown drain 55s so in-flight submits get recorded, watcher panics isolated per tick, advisory lock guard releases on cancel/panic.

Observability: payment.settled_unrecorded and reserve.payout_failures metrics, reserve.* outbox events, unrecordable-settlement error logs, forecast/low-water endpoint, GET /admin/exchange-reserve on-chain snapshot for manual drift repair (adjustment/held_adjustment entries).

gaps.title: (a) /managed-account/sign has no idempotency key and no write-ahead intent; a 408/500 after Horizon accepts the tx loses the bookkeeping and invites a second payment
gaps.detail: managed_seed.rs:546-588: sign+submit, then INSERT after settlement, error swallowed; SignSubmitRequest (models.rs:256-262) has no key; TimeoutLayer (main.rs:789) drops the future mid-flight; impalactl ambiguous.go:13-19 already warns users. The reserve drivers show the right shape (intent row + guarded state + stale sweep) but even they do not persist the PreparedTx hash before submit (reserve_watch.rs:1278-1285 leaves stellar_tx_hash NULL; admin_reserve.rs:1885-1893 reads it and finds None), although signer.rs:52-62/82-88 already exposes prepare_payment/submit_prepared for exactly that.
gaps.suggested_approach: Migration 037_custodial_payment_intent.sql: CREATE TABLE custodial_payment_intent (intent_id UUID PK DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), payala_account_id VARCHAR(64) REFERENCES impala_account ON DELETE SET NULL, source_account VARCHAR(56) NOT NULL, idempotency_key VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL, request_fingerprint VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL /* sha256 hex over canonical destination|amount_minor|asset|memo|fee */, destination VARCHAR(69) NOT NULL, asset VARCHAR(12) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'XLM', amount_minor BIGINT NOT NULL CHECK (amount_minor > 0), memo VARCHAR(28), fee_stroops INTEGER, sequence BIGINT, stellar_hash VARCHAR(64), status VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'preparing' CHECK (status IN ('preparing','submitting','settled','rejected','unknown')), last_error VARCHAR(200), btxid UUID REFERENCES transaction ON DELETE SET NULL, created_at, updated_at, resolved_at); UNIQUE (payala_account_id, idempotency_key) — scoped per account like payala_sync_item (027:54-57); CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_custodial_intent_hash ON (stellar_hash) WHERE stellar_hash IS NOT NULL; partial index on (status, created_at) WHERE status IN ('submitting','unknown') for the sweep; optionally widen chk_transaction_origin with 'custodial_sign' via DROP + ADD NOT VALID + VALIDATE (031:179-183 pattern) and add TX_ORIGIN_CUSTODIAL_SIGN + a models.rs drift test. Key semantics: accept `idempotency_key` as an appended optional body field (openapi append-only) or `Idempotency-Key` header; generate server-side UUID if absent (documented as non-replayable). Handler flow: parse amount with parse_decimal_to_minor(…,7) (reserve.rs:660) -> in one tx: pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('custodial_sign:'||account)); INSERT intent ON CONFLICT (account,key) DO NOTHING RETURNING; if conflict: SELECT existing — fingerprint mismatch -> 422; settled -> replay 200 {stellar_hash, btxid, intent_id} with header Idempotent-Replayed: true; rejected -> replay the 400; preparing/submitting/unknown -> 409 {status, intent_id, stellar_hash?} and NEVER resubmit; commit -> load_protected_seed -> signer.prepare_payment -> UPDATE intent SET stellar_hash,sequence,status='submitting' WHERE intent_id AND status='preparing' -> submit_prepared -> classify_submit: Settled -> one tx {INSERT transaction (…, account_id, origin) , UPDATE intent settled+btxid, emit_event new AccountEvent::CustodialPaymentSettled{account_id, intent_id, btxid, stellar_hash, amount_minor}}; Rejected -> status rejected + last_error -> 400; Ambiguous -> status unknown -> 503 body {status:'unknown', intent_id, stellar_hash, message:'do not retry; poll'}. Add GET /managed-account/intents/{intent_id} (owner) for polling. Crash/408 recovery: an hourly-or-faster sweep (server task like reserve_watch, or piggyback the watcher) selects intents in 'submitting'/'unknown' older than 600s (>= 2×TX_TIMEOUT_SECS), calls Horizon GET /transactions/{hash} (fetch_transaction_payments horizon.rs:243 already parses transaction_successful) -> settled (insert the transaction row + event) or, once head_is_fresh (horizon.rs:232) and time bounds have passed, rejected('expired'). Also consider running submit+record inside a detached tokio task awaited by the handler so the TimeoutLayer cancelling the request does not cancel the record step. Recount every bind (sqlx hazard) and add a string-pin test that the INSERT column list matches the migration; update impalactl `transfer send` to mint a UUID key and reuse it on retry, replacing the ambiguous.go warning path with a poll.

gaps.title: (b) No per-account daily limit, per-tx cap, or global custodial pause on the sign path
gaps.detail: Only the 5/min rate limit bounds a compromised owner token or a bad client loop (managed_seed.rs:521-528); nothing bounds value per request or per day, and there is no brake an operator can pull without redeploying (the only precedents are reserve-side: refunds_enabled, replenish policy caps, quote kill switch). A pause must be fail-closed and DB-authoritative; Redis already fails closed for the rate limit but a pause flag must never read as 'unknown -> allowed'.
gaps.suggested_approach: Same migration 037 (or 038): CREATE TABLE custodial_policy (id BOOLEAN PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT true CHECK (id), paused BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false, paused_by VARCHAR(64), paused_at TIMESTAMPTZ, pause_reason VARCHAR(200), per_tx_max_stroops BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (>=0), per_account_daily_max_stroops BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (>=0), updated_by, updated_at) seeded with one row; ALTER TABLE impala_account ADD custodial_daily_max_stroops BIGINT NULL (per-account override, NULL = global). House convention: 0 = unconfigured -> refuse (032:6-10), so document the deploy order: migrate, PUT the caps, then roll the binary. Enforcement inside the intent transaction from (a): SELECT paused, caps FROM custodial_policy FOR SHARE; if paused -> 503 'custodial signing paused' before load_protected_seed; amount_minor <= per_tx_max; SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount_minor),0) FROM custodial_payment_intent WHERE payala_account_id=$1 AND status IN ('submitting','settled','unknown') AND created_at >= now()-interval '24 hours' (rolling window like DAILY_REFUND_SPEND_SQL; 'unknown' counts as spent — fail closed) + amount_minor <= daily cap, all under the per-account advisory lock so concurrent requests cannot both pass. Endpoints: PUT /admin/custody/policy (caps) and POST /admin/custody/pause under Privileged<ManageReserve> (admin+treasurer: any money-ops role may pull the brake); POST /admin/custody/resume under AdminUser (governance) — or introduce Capability::ManageCustody, which requires editing auth.rs::role_has_capability, impala-ui/html/js/roles.js and tests/fixtures/role-capabilities.json together and will trip every_privileged_handler_takes_its_exact_capability until the handler list is updated. Emit outbox events custody.paused / custody.resumed / custody.policy_updated (append-only vocabulary; actor in account_id). Optionally gate drive_payouts/drive_refunds/drive_replenishment on the same paused flag (start nothing new, like the cancel-token check at reserve_watch.rs:1238) as a global brake. Add a tripwire test that include_str!s managed_seed.rs and asserts the pause/limit check text precedes 'load_protected_seed(' in sign_and_submit (auth.rs:919 pattern). Rate limit remains as-is; document in openapi and impalactl (new 503 reason).

gaps.title: (c) No liabilities-vs-reserves report; custodial positions are not enumerable and Payala/card figures are self-reported or absent
gaps.detail: Reserve drift is only visible as two strings in GET /admin/exchange-reserve; managed_seed rows have no listing endpoint; transaction rows carry no Stellar amount; payala_reserve is client-asserted; card balances never reach the bridge; nothing runs daily.
gaps.suggested_approach: Add GET /admin/reconciliation/positions (Privileged<ReadReserve> so auditor+treasurer+admin can read; consider a dedicated ReadReconciliation later) returning: {as_of, horizon:{url, head_closed_at, lag_secs, fresh}, reserve:{buckets:[{currency, available_minor, held_minor, ledger_total_minor, onchain_minor (parse_decimal_to_minor of the Horizon balance), drift_minor = onchain - ledger_total, trustline}], obligations:{refunds_queued_minor, refunds_needs_review_minor, refunds_frozen_minor, payout_intents_open (payout_attempt without fulfillment), cycles_in_flight_spend_minor, fiat_in_transit_cents}, journal_replay_ok (SUM(delta)/SUM(held_delta) per currency == bucket columns)}, custodial:{accounts, addresses_checked, onchain:{XLM_stroops, per stablecoin minor}, unreachable:[G...], intents_unknown, intents_settled_24h_minor}, payala:{source:'self_reported', accounts_with_reserve, net_per_currency (SUM(payala_reserve.balance) GROUP BY currency), last_batch_at}, card:{source:'none'}, invariants:[{name:'reserve_chain_covers_ledger', ok, detail}, {name:'reserve_available_covers_open_obligations', ok}, {name:'custodial_addresses_funded', ok}]}. Data sources: conversion_reserve + conversion_reserve_entry + conversion_reserve_refund + conversion_reserve_replenishment; managed_seed (SELECT payala_account_id, stellar_account_id ORDER BY id LIMIT/offset — bound Horizon fan-out with a page size and buffer_unordered like cron_sync); custodial_payment_intent from (a) for amounts (the transaction table cannot supply them). Persist a daily snapshot: table reconciliation_snapshot(snapshot_id, as_of, payload JSONB, drift_detected BOOLEAN) written by a server-side task at a fixed UTC hour under an advisory lock (RESERVE_WATCHER_LOCK_KEY pattern), emitting outbox event reconciliation.drift_detected {currency, drift_minor} when |drift| > a per-bucket tolerance column (0 = alert on any drift). Surface in impala-ui reserve page and impalactl (`reserve positions --json`, append-only schema with golden file). Explicitly label Payala figures as unverifiable and card as out of scope in the response.

gaps.title: (d) Conservation specification document is missing
gaps.detail: Operators and reviewers rely on scattered module docs (reserve_watch.rs:1-36, migration 031/032 headers, conversion-reserve.md) and on tripwire tests; no single document names each state's owner, idempotency anchor, and crash-recovery path, and the custodial path is undocumented beyond openapi and the impalactl warning.
gaps.suggested_approach: Add docs/conservation-spec.md (link from ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/runbooks/README.md) with: 1) Domains and authoritative owners — Stellar ledger (Horizon = truth; bridge holds keys for custodial + reserve accounts); bridge Postgres (transaction, managed_seed, custodial_payment_intent, conversion_reserve*, payala_reserve/payala_sync_*, event_outbox); Payala backend (external, never called; only client-asserted batches); card (on-card int64, invisible to the bridge). 2) Units and the one conversion boundary (parse_decimal_to_minor/minor_to_decimal_string). 3) As-is state machines with owner / anchor / recovery / event / pinning test per transition: (i) custodial sign: request -> seed decrypt -> prepare -> submit -> transaction row [today: no intent, retry re-pays; after (a): preparing -> submitting(hash) -> settled|rejected|unknown -> sweep]; (ii) reserve order: quote_hold|hold (RESERVE_HOLD_SQL, advisory lock per account) -> awaiting_deposit -> deposit (paging_token anchor) -> processing -> payout_attempt (UNIQUE(order_id,kind)) -> completed (fulfillment, transaction row, ReserveFulfilled) | on_hold (freeze: submit_unknown|max_attempts|stale_intent) -> admin resolve complete|fail|retry (chain-verified) ; expiry -> hold_release; disburse shape -> awaiting_disbursement -> disbursement; (iii) refund obligation: unmatched/deposit -> queue_refund (UNIQUE source_paging_token) needs_review|queued -> inflight (CLAIM CAS + refund_intent debit, daily cap) -> sent | queued/failed (refund_reversal) | frozen (stale_claim/submit_unknown) | cancelled; (iv) replenishment cycle: planned (uq_crr_inflight) -> creating -> created -> sending (replenish_attempt) -> sent (replenish_sent) -> completed (replenish_credit) | refunded | failed (abort, release) | frozen; usdc_to_usd: in_transit -> fiat_confirmed | fiat_written_off; (v) payala sync: batch -> payala_sync_item PK -> reserve net upsert | mirror rows (uq_transaction_payala_sync) — no on-chain effect; (vi) outbox: emit in-tx -> fan_out (UNIQUE webhook_id,event_id) -> leased delivery -> delivered|failed. 4) Invariants: available+held replays from the journal; chain >= ledger per bucket; one payout per order; one credit per paging_token; one obligation per payment; cursor monotonic; no plaintext seed at rest; ambiguous submits are never resubmitted. 5) Failure-injection matrix (the B6 list) naming the pinning tests and the 'no test' cells as backlog (duplicate sign, DB rollback, Horizon partition on sign, card/backend conflicts, partial withdrawal, signer compromise rotation). 6) Controls inventory (caps, switches, rate limits, roles). 7) Reconciliation procedure and the report from (c). 8) Open gaps and owners. Pin the doc with a test that include_str!s it and asserts every journal kind in VALID_RESERVE_ENTRY_KINDS and every intent status appears, so vocabulary drift breaks CI.

gaps.title: Reserve drivers do not persist the prepared tx hash before submit, so ambiguous outcomes are resolved by memo/amount search instead of exact hash
gaps.detail: reserve_watch.rs:1278-1285, 1945-1956 and replenish.rs submit_spend write intents without stellar_tx_hash and call sign_and_submit_payment; admin_reserve.rs:1885-1893 reads the intent hash (None) and falls back to find_onchain_payout (1762). signer.rs:52-56 documents PreparedTx exactly for this.
gaps.suggested_approach: Split each driver into prepare_payment -> UPDATE the intent entry SET stellar_tx_hash = prepared.stellar_hash (journal rows are append-only, so instead write the hash on a new nullable column of exchange_order/refund/cycle, or add a 'payout_prepared' journal kind with the hash — the CHECK widening and models drift test apply) -> submit_prepared. Then resolve_intent_by_hash (admin_reserve.rs:2228) becomes the primary path and the sweep can settle frozen orders automatically by hash lookup.

gaps.title: Outbox atomicity exceptions and missing events
gaps.detail: admin_keys.rs:552-577 and 868-882 emit credential import/revoke events in a separate transaction after the state change; custodial sign settlements and payala_sync mirror rows emit no event; flush_unmatched_summaries is post-commit by design.
gaps.suggested_approach: Pass the store::insert_version/revoke_active transaction into emit_event (or have the store functions accept &mut Transaction) so the audit event commits with the row; add CustodialPaymentSettled (from gap a) and, optionally, a payala_sync.batch_applied event with counts only (no memo/digest).

gaps.title: No enumerable custodial position and no amount on transaction rows
gaps.detail: managed_seed is only looked up by id; transaction rows from sign_and_submit carry no amount, destination, or account_id (managed_seed.rs:563-571), so per-account spend cannot be derived from the ledger.
gaps.suggested_approach: Record amount_minor/destination on custodial_payment_intent (gap a) and set transaction.account_id on the sign path; add GET /admin/custody/accounts (ReadAccounts or ReadReserve) listing managed_seed (payala_account_id, stellar_account_id, origin, format_version, created_at) with an optional Horizon balance column, bounded per page.

constraints: cargo test runs with no Postgres/Redis: SQL is pinned by string/tripwire tests only, so every new statement needs a shape-pin test and every INSERT bind count must be recounted by hand (sqlx dynamic queries; three consecutive Option<Uuid> binds transpose silently).
cargo clippy -- -D warnings is the CI gate; new handlers with >7 args need #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)] like sign_and_submit.

Migrations are operator-invoked (RUN_MODE=migrate) and must run before the binary that depends on them; next number is 037; CHECK widening must use DROP + ADD ... NOT VALID + VALIDATE (031:169-183); new columns must be nullable or defaulted so existing shared INSERTs keep working; sqlx wraps each migration in a transaction (no CONCURRENTLY).

House money rules: i64 minor units only (parse_decimal_to_minor / minor_to_decimal_string are the sole boundary), guarded single-statement UPDATEs with UNIQUE idempotency anchors, write-ahead intents before submits, fail closed on ambiguity, '0 = unconfigured -> refuse' for caps, metrics only after commit, never resubmit an ambiguous transaction (TX_TIMEOUT_SECS=300; stale thresholds >= 600s).

Request budget: TimeoutLayer 30s (REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS) returns 408 and drops the handler future; statement_timeout 60s; SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_DEADLINE_SECS=55; Horizon client timeout 30s — any new sign flow must survive cancellation between submit and record.

RBAC: role/capability semantics change only by editing auth.rs::role_has_capability, impala-ui/html/js/roles.js and impala-ui/tests/fixtures/role-capabilities.json together; privileged handlers must use the exact Privileged<Cap>/AdminUser extractor by name or auth.rs tripwires (migration_035_matches_all_roles, extractor_swap_is_complete_per_module, every_privileged_handler_takes_its_exact_capability) fail; ALL_ROLES must match migration 035's CHECK.

Append-only contracts: openapi.yaml, event_outbox payload shapes (no PII/secrets, no addresses/memos in reserve events), lumencli/impalactl --json/--csv schemas with golden files; new fields must be additive and optional.
Constants/DDL drift tests in models.rs must be extended for any new CHECK vocabulary (intent status, transaction origin, event kinds); VARCHAR widths are runtime failures (22001) on money paths.

Key custody: nothing may return, log, or event secret bytes; the reserve seed stays generate-only; the reserve account must remain quarantined from /managed-account/* via ReserveAccountGuard (configuration-keyed); custodial signing must stay synchronous and server-only (never the SQS worker).
Redis is fail-closed for auth/rate limits and must not become the authority for a money pause flag; Postgres single-row state tables (id BOOLEAN PK CHECK(id)) are the precedent for global switches.
impala-ui: no build step, IIFE modules, EscapeHtml.escape for dynamic HTML (no attribute interpolation), Vitest in node without jsdom — new UI surfaces need DOM-free pure modules.
Do not run git checkout -- <file> during experiments; the working tree carries uncommitted changes across many files.

flow.area: End-to-end value flow and cross-domain conservation: Stellar/USDC on-chain, Soroban MultisigUsdcWrapper, bridge custodial accounts + conversion reserve, Payala backend (sync/payala, TCP listener, migration 027), and the smartcard offline balance (myBalance / SIGN_TRANSFER / VERIFY_TRANSFER) including the Android demo and impala-lib clients.
flow.summary: Five value domains exist; only two are wired together by code. (1) Stellar: the bridge signs XLM payments from per-user custodial seeds (managed_seed.rs, settle-then-record, no idempotency key) and USDC/USDT0/XLM from one generate-only reserve seed (reserve_watch/replenish/admin_reserve) behind write-ahead intents, guarded single-statement SQL and an append-only journal that mirrors the reserve's Stellar account. (2) Soroban MultisigUsdcWrapper holds USDC in instance storage with per-address balances; nothing in the bridge calls it — SOROBAN_CONTRACT_ID is only logged/surfaced, and /sync + stellar_reconcile merely match RPC tx ids against `transaction` rows. (3) Bridge DB: conversion_reserve buckets (chain-mirrored, anchored) and payala_reserve (self-asserted, quarantined). (4) Payala backend: known to the bridge only as owner-signed JSON batches via POST /sync/payala (idempotent PK, no signature or counterparty verification) and as unauthenticated raw TCP JSON events cached in Redis that nothing consumes. (5) Card: myBalance is 8 EEPROM bytes; SIGN_TRANSFER debits atomically, VERIFY_TRANSFER credits from ANY secp256r1 key (pubKeySig unchecked) under a per-recipient strictly-increasing counter; cards cannot be personalized (accountId/currency are never written), and no Android, impala-lib or bridge code calls either transfer INS. There is no load, no redemption and no cross-domain conservation; of the reviewer's six target transitions, two are partially present on isolated islands and four are absent.

claims.evidence: No code moves value from Stellar/bridge INTO a card balance. The only on-card credit is INS_VERIFY_TRANSFER (ImpalaApplet.java:459-462, 891-963), which needs a 60-byte signable naming the card as recipient plus any secp256r1 signature; nothing produces one: the Android reader exposes only identity/auth INS (ImpalaCardReader.kt:73-80), BridgeApiService.kt has no load endpoint (lines 84-95, 161-162), impala-lib NfcContactActivity sends only the tag UID as an APDU (NfcContactActivity.java:89-90), and a repo-wide grep for VERIFY_TRANSFER/SIGN_TRANSFER/verifyTransfer/signTransfer outside impala-card returns nothing. The bridge card table has no balance column (008_create_card.sql:2-13).

No code moves card balance back to Stellar. INS_SIGN_TRANSFER debits myBalance and returns [sig72|pubkey65|zero72] (ImpalaApplet.java:812-877); no bridge route accepts that tuple (main.rs:547-644 route table; card_auth.rs:261-263 only verifies SIGN_AUTH over IMPALA-AUTH: domain), and managed_seed.rs sign_and_submit (507-615) takes destination/amount from the JWT owner with no reference to any card, counter or offline balance. POST /transaction (transaction.rs:112-139) records ids only; the demo posts it without an amount (TransfersFragment.kt:108-113).

Reserve-side transitions have unique ids, idempotency anchors, crash recovery and a journal (031 §UNIQUE 100-105; reserve_watch.rs:1267-1305 write-ahead intent; 2246-2286 stale sweeps; admin_reserve.rs:2095-2174 chain-verified resolve). The user custodial path has a tx hash but no idempotency anchor and settle-then-record (managed_seed.rs:551-588). Payala balances have an idempotency PK (027:58-68) but no verification. Card transitions have atomicity (JCSystem, ImpalaApplet.java:860-869, 954-957) and a receive counter (942-947) but no persisted id, receipt or journal; sender-side has no replay guard at all.

The domains are not connected by code, so one unit cannot be double-counted ACROSS domains — but no conservation is enforced either. Inside the card domain one unit is multiply spendable: verifyTransfer trusts the pubkey in the tail (ImpalaApplet.java:887-889, 904) and every card's accountId is all zeros (never written; apdu.md:82-96), so one signable with recipient=0x00*16 and counter n credits every card whose lastReceiveCounter < n (AppletInteropTest.kt:90-104 funds a card from an ad-hoc JCA key). Payala side: /sync/payala takes signed amounts on the owner's word with no counterparty netting (sync.rs:288-455; SECURITY.md:229-241).

Of the target machine, RESERVED_FOR_OFFLINE_ISSUANCE and PENDING_ONCHAIN_RELEASE have no implementation for user/card value (closest primitives: RESERVE_HOLD_SQL reserve.rs:57-61 and the payout intent reserve_watch.rs:1267-1305, both reserve-only). OFFLINE_SPENDABLE→OFFLINE_TRANSFERRED exists on-card only (signTransfer/verifyTransfer) with no coordinator in repo; OFFLINE_TRANSFERRED→RECONCILED exists as unverified bookkeeping (sync.rs:369-455). See facts 'AS-IS state machine' and 'TARGET state machine mapping'.

The bridge never calls wrap/schedule_unwrap/execute_*: SOROBAN_CONTRACT_ID is parsed (config.rs:655-657), logged (main.rs:275-276) and surfaced by GET /network (network.rs:17); sync_account_core (sync.rs:69-112) and jobs/stellar_reconcile.rs:25-85 POST getTransactions with empty params and only match tx ids against `transaction.stellar_tx_id`. ARCHITECTURE.md:34-43 Use Case 2 step 3 ('the bridge's Stellar reconciliation job detects the scheduled operation') is not implemented — no event decoding, no contract read.

No Payala backend code is in this repo. The bridge's only inputs are owner-asserted batches (models.rs:306-320; sync.rs:288-580) and raw JSON over an unauthenticated TCP listener stored to Redis keys payala:event:{ts}:{uuid} / payala:latest_event (streams.rs:288-401) that no reader consumes. Whether Payala keeps a ledger, how card counters are allocated, or whether Payala debits anything when a card is credited cannot be decided here.

facts.fact: wrap(env, signers, depositor, amount): verify_multisig + depositor.require_auth, then token_client.transfer(depositor -> contract) (line 290), Balance(depositor) += amount (292-298), WrappedUsdc.total_wrapped += amount (300-306), event ('wrap', depositor) amount (308-309). Immediate; no id, no idempotency — each call moves real USDC into the contract.

schedule_unwrap returns a sequential u64 timelock_id (NextTimeLockId, 354-358, 380-383); the balance check at 347-352 is advisory only (module doc 23-30: multiple timelocks may over-schedule one balance). execute_unwrap (394-463) re-checks balance (415-420), sets executed=true before the external transfer (422-426), burns Balance (432-435), transfers USDC out (441), decrements total_wrapped (443-449) and REMOVES the TimeLock so replay panics 'Timelock not found' (455-457). schedule_transfer/execute_transfer (470-613) do the same for internal balances; cancel_timelock (616-641) removes the entry.

POST /sync (admin) and jobs/stellar_reconcile.rs:25-85 send Soroban RPC getTransactions with `params: {}` and only intersect returned ids with `SELECT stellar_tx_id FROM transaction WHERE stellar_tx_id = ANY($1)` (SYNC_KNOWN_TX_SQL, line 28-29), logging matches at debug. No contract call, no balance read, no event decode; the Soroban wrapper is unobserved by the bridge.

POST /managed-account/sign: require_owner, reserve-account quarantine (49-61, 520), rate limit SIGN_RATE_LIMIT, then load_protected_seed (305-412: decrypt, unseal bound header, ASSERT derived address == managed_seed.stellar_account_id at 389-400) and sign_and_submit_payment with Asset::Native ONLY (line 542). No write-ahead row: the transaction row (btxid) is inserted only after settlement (561-573); a bookkeeping failure is logged + metric unrecorded_settled_payments (579-586) and still returns success. Comment 551-560: a client retry after a 5xx submits a SECOND real payment (fetch_sequence re-reads the advanced sequence).

managed_seed: one row per account, UNIQUE(payala_account_id) and UNIQUE(stellar_account_id); columns backend/ciphertext/wrapped_data_key/nonce/key_id/key_version/origin('generated'|'imported'); no balance column. Bridge-side balances for custodial accounts do not exist — GET /account/onchain (account.rs:182-218) reads Horizon live.

RESERVE_HOLD_SQL: UPDATE conversion_reserve SET available=available-$2, held=held+$2 WHERE currency=$1 AND available>=$2 AND (held+$2)*2 <= (available+held) RETURNING available, held, low_water. RESERVE_BUCKET_APPLY_SQL (65-68): both columns must stay >=0 or zero rows. RESERVE_ENTRY_INSERT_SQL (78-82) is the ONE journal insert (17 columns) bound only through JournalEntry/journal_insert (94-148). ORDER_HOLD_SQL (159-168) finds an order's hold via its own `hold` entry OR its consumed quote's hold_minor.

conversion_reserve(currency PK, minor_scale, available>=0, held>=0, low_water); conversion_reserve_entry journal (70-98) with kinds hold/hold_release/deposit/unmatched_deposit/payout_attempt/fulfillment/disbursement/topup/withdrawal/adjustment/held_adjustment (widened by 032:341-354 with quote_*, replenish_*, offramp_*, fiat_*, refund_*), balance_after/held_after snapshots; anchors: UNIQUE(order_id,kind) WHERE order_id NOT NULL (100-102), UNIQUE(paging_token) (104-106); conversion_reserve_state single row horizon_cursor (118-121); conversion_reserve_unmatched PK paging_token (128-145). transaction.origin widened to include 'conversion_reserve' (176-183). Buckets seeded USDC(7), USD(2), XLM(7); 036 adds USDT0(7).

run_creation_tx: pg_advisory_xact_lock('conv_reserve:'||account) (1332), open-order cap RESERVE_MAX_OPEN_ORDERS_PER_ACCOUNT=3 (1338-1346), RESERVE_HOLD_SQL (1348-1357), exchange_order insert with provider='reserve', status awaiting_deposit, provider_order_id = payin memo = base32_order_ref(order_id) (26-char Crockford, 742-750), provider_payload {hold_currency, hold_minor, deposit_currency, shape,...} (1361-1376), journal `hold` entry delta=-hold held_delta=+hold (1404-1417), outbox event, commit.

QUOTE_CLAIM_SQL flips status open->consumed only when owner matches and expires_at > now (single statement, 59-65); mint_quote takes RESERVE_HOLD_SQL at mint time and writes `quote_hold` (208-264); divert_quoted_order writes a zero-delta `quote_consume` entry and links quote->order (416-482) — capacity never returns to available between quote and order. Expiry/retire write `quote_release` (548-595).

tick(): pg_try_advisory_lock RESERVE_WATCHER_LOCK_KEY=0x494d5052535256 45 via sqlx PgAdvisoryLock guard (397-424); tick_inner order (451-483): drain_deposits -> (if chain OK) drive_payouts, drive_refunds -> freeze_stale_intents, freeze_stale_refunds -> (if chain OK) expire_stale_orders -> expire_stale_quotes -> (if chain OK) replenish::drive_replenishment -> freeze_stale_cycles. Money-correctness does not depend on the lock (module doc 31-36).

process_payment: FIRST checks EXISTS(entry.paging_token=$1) OR EXISTS(unmatched.paging_token=$1) (827-837) so a replayed Horizon page is a no-op even if classification changed; cycle-ref memos go to replenish::credit_cycle_arrival (846-887); order memo lookup by provider_order_id=UPPER(TRIM(memo)) (891-905); classify_deposit (759-813) yields Match{overpaid}/Unmatched{late|underpaid|wrong_asset|no_match}/Ignore, requiring p.to == reserve address and asset pinned by bucket_for_asset(code,issuer). apply_deposit (944-1077): guarded UPDATE exchange_order awaiting_deposit->processing (959-976; loser becomes 'late' unmatched), credit ACTUAL amount (990-1000), `deposit` entry with paging_token+tx_hash+sender (1011-1037; 23505 => rollback no-op). Cursor advances only after a page's rows committed and only forward numerically (advance_cursor 682-692).

drive_one_payout: claim = INSERT `payout_attempt` (0/0, snapshots under FOR UPDATE) which UNIQUE(order_id,kind) admits once (1267-1305), or CAS provider_status payout_retry->payout_inflight (1252-1265); load reserve seed via managed_seed::load_protected_seed (1339-1345); asset from reserve.asset_for_bucket(payout_bucket_for_hold_currency) else freeze (1349-1365); memo = payout_extra_id or order ref (1372-1377); classify_submit (158-171): Ok=>Settled, BadRequest=>Rejected{permanent if op_no_trust/op_no_destination/op_line_full/op_not_authorized}, Retryable=>Rejected non-permanent (pre-submit), anything else=>Ambiguous. Settled -> record_fulfillment (1459-1568: order CAS processing|on_hold->completed/paid, held -= amount, `fulfillment` entry, transaction row origin conversion_reserve + btxid link, event); Rejected -> retry with backoff up to RESERVE_MAX_PAYOUT_ATTEMPTS=5 then on_hold; Ambiguous -> freeze_on_hold (1573-1611), never resubmitted. STALE_INTENT_SECS=600 >= 2*TX_TIMEOUT_SECS(300) (70-74).

[Soroban] Active<->Paused; per address: (USDC external) --wrap--> Balance(addr) --schedule_unwrap(id)--> TimeLock(id) --execute_unwrap--> (USDC external) | --cancel--> Balance ; Balance --schedule_transfer/execute_transfer--> Balance(other). Bridge: unobserved.
