gaps.title: No issuance (load) or redemption path exists between chain/bridge and the card balance
gaps.detail: There is no code that (a) debits a chain or custodial balance and produces a card-acceptable credit, or (b) accepts a card debit proof and credits chain. The card can be credited by any secp256r1 key (ImpalaApplet.java:887-889, 904) and cannot be personalized (accountId never written; apdu.md:82-96), so even a future bridge issuer could not address a specific card. The bridge stores no per-card balance, counter, issuer key or issuance intent (008_create_card.sql). Value in the card domain is therefore unbacked by construction, and value in the chain domain is never reserved for offline use.
gaps.suggested_approach: Bridge repo: (1) add an `offline_issuance` table with write-ahead intent (issuance_id, card_id, account_id, currency, amount_minor, counter, state RESERVED->ISSUED->ACK|REVERSED, UNIQUE(card_id, counter)) funded by a guarded hold on a chain-mirrored bucket (reuse RESERVE_HOLD_SQL/JournalEntry shape or a per-account ledger); (2) an issuer keypair installed via /admin/keys (fingerprint-only responses) that signs the 60-byte signable with recipient=card accountId and a bridge-allocated per-card monotonic counter; (3) a redemption endpoint accepting (signable, sig, pubkey) verified against card.ec_pubkey with UNIQUE(card_id, sender counter/hashable) and a write-ahead release row before any on-chain submit, reusing classify_submit/freeze/resolve. Card repo (out of bridge scope but prerequisite): personalization command for accountId/currency, pin the issuer pubkey (verify pubKeySig on-card or an allowlist), and persist a sender-side counter + last hashable.

gaps.title: Card-to-card transfer is not conservation-safe: one debit can credit many recipients and any key can mint
gaps.detail: verifyTransfer checks only sig-over-signable, sender!=me, recipient==me, counter>last (ImpalaApplet.java:906-947); pubKeySig is ignored and no issuer/allowlist exists. All cards share accountId 0x00*16, so one signable credits every card. signTransfer persists no counter and discards the hashable (855-858), so a sender can sign the same signable repeatedly and a coordinator can fan one signature out to N recipients with fresh counters (counter scope is per-recipient, 933-941). AppletInteropTest.kt:90-104 shows minting from an ad-hoc key.
gaps.suggested_approach: Card side: verify pubKeySig against a pinned program/issuer key (the field already rides in the 209-byte tail), persist a sender counter and require counter == last+1 for outgoing, bind recipient to a personalized accountId. Bridge side: treat card balance as unverified until a bridge-verified redemption exists; never let payala_reserve or card-derived numbers gate on-chain movement (already documented in SECURITY.md:229-241, keep it).

gaps.title: Payala reconciliation is self-asserted and never netted across counterparties
gaps.detail: POST /sync/payala accepts signed i64 amounts on the JWT owner's word; the PK is per (account, tx) precisely because both parties post the same id with opposite signs (027:54-57), but nothing checks that the two postings exist or net to zero, that the amount matches a card signature, or that the counter was consumed. payala_reserve may go negative (027:22-24). Mode flips with force=true leave prior balances in place (admin.rs:291-311). The Android demo never calls this endpoint; impalactl is the only client.
gaps.suggested_approach: Bridge: extend PayalaSyncItemInput with the 60-byte signable + DER signature + sender/recipient card ids; verify against card.ec_pubkey (aws_lc_rs already used in card_auth.rs), dedupe on (sender_card, counter) and (recipient_card, counter), and net counterparties by payala_tx_id into a `payala_transfer` row with two legs; keep the quarantine until a redemption path consumes reconciled balances. External (Payala backend): define the authoritative transfer record and counter allocation so the bridge can verify rather than trust.

gaps.title: Payala TCP listener is unauthenticated, schema-less and unconsumed
gaps.detail: payala_stream (streams.rs:288-401) accepts any TCP peer, parses one read as one JSON message, and stores raw text in Redis (payala:event:*, payala:latest_event). No reader exists, no auth/HMAC, no schema, no DB durability. ARCHITECTURE.md:253/289 presents it as the Payala integration.
gaps.suggested_approach: Either remove it from the value story (document as telemetry only) or replace with an authenticated, HMAC-verified ingest (exchange_webhook.rs:78-152 precedent verifies HMAC over the raw body before parsing) that writes durable rows and feeds the verified reconciliation above. External: Payala must define the event contract.

gaps.title: User custodial payments have no write-ahead intent or idempotency key
gaps.detail: POST /managed-account/sign submits first and records after (managed_seed.rs:546-588); a client retry after a timeout/5xx produces a second real payment (551-560). The reserve path already has the correct pattern (intent row -> submit -> classify -> record; stale freeze).
gaps.suggested_approach: Add an idempotency key (client-supplied or hash of destination+amount+memo+sequence) with a write-ahead `custodial_payment_intent` row UNIQUE(account_id, idempotency_key) inserted before submit and updated by classify_submit; expose the intent id so a retry returns the same result. Needed before any offline redemption can release on-chain safely.

gaps.title: Soroban wrapper is not integrated; ARCHITECTURE overclaims
gaps.detail: No bridge code calls or observes MultisigUsdcWrapper; /sync and stellar_reconcile only match RPC tx ids. ARCHITECTURE.md:34-43 (Use Case 2 step 3) claims timelock detection. Contract-side, wrap has no idempotency and schedule does not reserve balance (lib.rs:23-30) — a bridge that used the wrapper as the RESERVED state would need execute-time failure handling.
gaps.suggested_approach: Decide whether the wrapper is in the value path. If yes: add a Soroban event consumer keyed by (contract, timelock_id) with UNIQUE anchors and use schedule_*/execute_* as the RESERVED/PENDING_ONCHAIN_RELEASE legs with execute-failure reconciliation; if no: correct ARCHITECTURE.md and keep SOROBAN_CONTRACT_ID informational.

gaps.title: Manual reserve entries and disbursements have no external anchor
gaps.detail: create_entry topup/withdrawal/adjustment (admin_reserve.rs:321-420) and disburse_order (1642-1752, up to 2x hold) are admin-asserted with rate limit + audit only; the runbook (conversion-reserve.md:133-142) warns a topup after a watched inflow double-books.
gaps.suggested_approach: Require an anchor on topup/withdrawal (stellar_tx_hash verified via verify_settlement_hash, or external_ref UNIQUE for bank legs) and add a periodic chain-vs-ledger drift check that emits an event when available+held != on-chain (the snapshot logic in get_status 163-199 already computes the inputs).

gaps.title: Minimal honest conservation specification for this system (what it must state)
gaps.detail: Given the code as it is, an honest spec must say: (S1) Chain is authoritative for Stellar balances; the bridge's conversion_reserve is a mirror that must satisfy available+held == on-chain balance per bucket except for admin-asserted USD and manual entries, checked by the drift snapshot. (S2) The Soroban wrapper is a separate on-chain ledger with no bridge mirror. (S3) payala_reserve, mirror rows and POST /transaction are UNVERIFIED client assertions with no value; they must never gate any on-chain movement. (S4) Card myBalance is a per-card counter with no issuer binding; the sum over cards is unbounded and unbacked; any card credit is mintable by any key. (S5) There is no state in which one unit is simultaneously represented in two domains because no transition crosses a domain boundary; conservation is therefore vacuously unenforced, not enforced. (S6) Any future issuance must create the offline unit only after a guarded, journaled hold exists on a chain-mirrored bucket, and any redemption must release on-chain only from a write-ahead intent that names the consumed card proof.
gaps.suggested_approach: In scope for the bridge repo: S1 drift check, S3 quarantine tests (tripwire that no handler reads payala_reserve or transaction.payala_amount on a signing path), issuance/redemption tables and endpoints, custodial idempotency, verified sync items. External / other repos: card personalization + issuer-key pinning (impala-card), Payala backend transfer/counter contract and authenticated event feed, and the decision whether the Soroban wrapper participates.

constraints: Money is integer minor units (i64/BIGINT, 7dp Stellar, 2dp USD); the only string<->minor boundary is reserve.rs parse_decimal_to_minor/minor_to_decimal_string; floats never touch money.

Every pool mutation is a guarded single-statement UPDATE plus a journal row under the same row lock, replayed idempotently via partial UNIQUE anchors; new transitions must add an anchor (order_id/quote_id/cycle_id/refund_id/paging_token pattern) and a `kind` <= 24 chars added to both the 032 CHECK and constants.rs VALID_RESERVE_ENTRY_KINDS (drift test).

RESERVE_ENTRY_INSERT_SQL is the single journal INSERT; widening it means editing JournalEntry + journal_insert, never a second positional INSERT (sqlx runtime queries do not check bind counts; no DB-executing tests exist — SQL is pinned by string tests only).

Write-ahead intent before any on-chain submit; only Horizon 400-with-result-codes (AppError::BadRequest) or pre-submit AppError::Retryable may be retried; everything else freezes for a human; resolution must verify chain state and fail closed when Horizon is lagging/inconclusive.

The reserve seed is generate-only and quarantined from /managed-account/*; all reserve signing goes through managed_seed::load_protected_seed (backend match + bound header + derived-address assertion) and takes the watcher advisory lock when racing the sequence number.
Migrations are operator-invoked (RUN_MODE=migrate) and must precede binaries that depend on them; CHECK changes use DROP + ADD ... NOT VALID + VALIDATE.

openapi.yaml, event-outbox payloads (events.rs, no PII/secrets) and lumencli JSON/CSV schemas are append-only contracts; new endpoints need openapi coverage and privileged handlers need the exact Privileged<Capability>/AdminUser extractor pinned by auth.rs tripwire tests.

Card wire contract is frozen for flashed CAPs: SIGNABLE_LENGTH=60 with the TransactionParser layout, SIGN_TRANSFER response 209 bytes, SIGN_TRANSFER not domain-tagged, SIGN_AUTH tagged 'IMPALA-AUTH:' (pinned by golden tests in card_auth.rs and AppletInteropTest.kt); receive counter is strictly-greater per recipient; INS 0x26 SET_CARD_DATA is declared but undispatched.
Card auth requires UUID account ids (16 raw RFC-4122 bytes in the signed message); a real card currently reports the nil UUID.

POST /sync/payala output (PayalaSyncResponse fields, batch/item/reserve tables) and sync_mode CHECK ('reserve','mirror') are pinned by tests; sync results are documented as quarantined from value movement (SECURITY.md) and any change must keep that until server-side verification exists.
Android demo has no build step for tests beyond gradle unit tests; impala-lib's IsoDep activity sends the raw tag UID as an APDU and must not be relied on for value operations.
All code must pass cargo clippy -D warnings; tests run without Postgres/Redis, so schema-vs-query drift is a runtime failure class.

docs.summary: The repo's marketing-level docs (README.md, ARCHITECTURE.md intro/use cases, impala-card/README.md, impala-soroban/README.md line 3, impala-bridge/README.md lines 3-10) describe an "offline payment → Stellar" bridge with hardware-backed transfers, RSA keys, 23 APDUs, Payala API correlation, bulk payments/escrow and "production-ready" infrastructure. The code is narrower: the applet (ImpalaApplet.java, 1135 lines) dispatches 17 application INS + 4 SCP03 INS; it implements card-local SIGN_TRANSFER (atomic debit) and VERIFY_TRANSFER (atomic credit, strictly-increasing per-recipient receive counter) that work with no network, but ignores the issuer signature over the sender key, has no accountId personalization command, and has no RSA key. The bridge verifies only SIGN_AUTH challenge signatures (card_auth.rs); it never sees transfer signatures, /sync/payala is client-asserted, stellar_reconcile only compares RPC tx ids, and nothing redeems a card balance on-chain. The honest documents are impala-card/docs/apdu.md, impala-bridge/SECURITY.md §Card/§Payala Sync, and impala-soroban/README.md §limitations; but SECURITY.md's admin section, ARCHITECTURE.md's card sections (timestamp SIGN_AUTH, GETDEL, CLA 0x80, RSA, SET_CARD_DATA, 4-tier RBAC) and CHANGELOG migration numbers are stale. There are zero git tags, no releases, no threat-model document (CONTRIBUTING points at a section that does not exist), no capability/evidence matrix, no known-limitations list, and no deployment manifest; nothing in the repo evidences physical-card or production testing.

signTransfer: data must be 4-byte PIN + 60-byte signable (:813); checks sender==accountId (:817-822, 0x6231), recipient!=accountId (:824-829, 0x6232), currency match if card currency non-zero (:833-839, 0x6229), amount<=balance (:841-844, 0x6224), counter non-negative (:846-849); signs 60 bytes UNTAGGED (:851, comment :803-805), then JCSystem transaction debits balance and bumps PIN-less counter (:860-870); response = DER sig in 72B slot ‖ 65B pubkey ‖ 8-byte DER zero sig in 72B slot (:872-876).
60-byte signable layout: dateTime(8)@0 | sender UUID(16)@8 | recipient UUID(16)@24 | currency(4)@40 | amount(4, big-endian, widened to int64)@44 | phoneId(8)@48 | counter(4)@56.

verifyTransfer: P1=0x00 buffers 60-byte signable in transient signableBuffer (:892-897); P1=0x01 needs 209-byte tail (:899-901), sets tempPubKey from tail bytes 72..137 (:904), verifies ECDSA over signable (:906-912, 0x0023), sender!=me (:915-920), recipient==me (:923-928), counter must be non-negative and strictly greater than lastReceiveCounter (:942-947, SW 0x6233), then atomic addToBalance + counter store (:954-957), then zeroes the buffered signable (:961). pubKeySig (tail bytes 137..208) is never read.

Counter scope comment: ONE receive stream per receiving card, not per sender; the sending side persists no counter — counters are allocated per recipient by an off-card 'transfer coordinator'; gaps allowed, repeats rejected, zero never accepted.

NOTE in code: 'verification trusts the public key embedded in the message tail — the trust chain on that key (pubKeySig) is established off-card, not by this applet.' No issuer/program public key is stored on the card (fields :143-184); Constants.SW_ERROR_KEY_VERIFICATION_FAILED 0x0022 is never thrown.

INS_INITIALIZE (0x2C) is unauthenticated (only failIfCardIsTerminated), one-shot (0x6686 on repeat), regenerates cardId and the P-256 keypair; accountId (:201) is never written by any dispatched command — it stays all-zeros for the card's life (apdu.md:86-94).

Factory defaults: master PIN 1-4-1-1-7-2-9-8 (10 tries), user PIN 1-1-1-1 (5 tries; OwnerPIN sized 5), SCP03 ENC/MAC/DEK all = GP test key 0x40..0x4F (:238-244) unless install TLV [0x01][flags][keys48?][masterPIN8 userPIN4?] overrides (:605-655); FLAG_INSTALL_ENFORCE=0x01 gates SIGN_TRANSFER/SIGN_AUTH with 0x6985 until a user PIN is provisioned.
APPLET_UPDATE (0x71, CLA 0x84 only): payload [seq(2)][len(2)][data]; only seq 0x0001 with len 48 is handled (rotates SCP03 ENC/MAC/DEK); every other seq is silently ignored (returns 0x9000).

gaps.title: Replace overstated 'offline payment / secure bridge / hardware-backed transfer' wording with threat-model-scoped claims
gaps.detail: README.md:3,7,11,48,55; ARCHITECTURE.md:5,7,21-32,40-41,944; impala-card/README.md:3-7; impala-soroban/README.md:3; impala-bridge/README.md:9-10 assert capabilities (offline payments crossing on-chain, bridge-verified card transfers, Payala API correlation, bulk payments/escrow, production readiness) that the code does not implement. The applet's real guarantee is card-local and conditional; the bridge's real guarantee is challenge-response login plus unverified bookkeeping.
gaps.suggested_approach:
Proposed replacement wording.
README.md:3 → "A custodial bridge whose server of record verifies smartcard login challenges, records client-asserted Payala transaction identifiers next to Stellar identifiers, and operates a USDC/USDT0 conversion reserve. The JavaCard applet implements a card-local balance with card-to-card debit/credit APDUs that work without a network; the bridge does not yet verify those transfer signatures, submit them on-chain, or reconcile card balances."
README.md:48 / ARCHITECTURE.md:7 (double-spend claim) → "Double-spend resistance, as implemented: a correctly personalized, non-compromised card atomically debits its local balance before releasing a transfer signature (ImpalaApplet.signTransfer: balance check → ECDSA sign → JCSystem transaction debit), and a receiving card rejects repeated or non-increasing 4-byte receive counters, crediting and advancing the counter in one JCSystem transaction (verifyTransfer). This property depends on: (1) the card's accountId being personalized — no APDU currently sets it; (2) the sender's public key being trustworthy — the applet does NOT verify the issuer signature over that key (pubKeySig is ignored), so any self-generated P-256 key is accepted; (3) the sender card being genuine — a cloned or emulated card can sign without debiting; (4) an off-card coordinator allocating strictly increasing counters per recipient — the sender persists no counter; (5) no reconciliation existing yet, so a violated assumption is not detected afterwards."
ARCHITECTURE.md:26 → "The app requests a single-use 32-byte challenge from the bridge and sends SIGN_AUTH with the raw challenge bytes."
ARCHITECTURE.md:29-32 → "The bridge stores both identifiers as an unverified record; no Stellar transaction is created by this flow. Only the login step is card-backed."
ARCHITECTURE.md:40-41 → delete, or: "No bridge component observes contract events today; stellar_reconcile only compares RPC transaction ids to local rows."
README.md:55 / ARCHITECTURE.md:944 → "Infrastructure-as-code: Terraform provisions … (validated in CI; no production deployment is recorded in this repository)."
impala-soroban/README.md:3 → "A multisig, time-locked USDC wrapper contract (wrap / schedule+execute unwrap or transfer / cancel / pause / rotate_signers)."
impala-bridge/README.md:9-10 → "The bridge accepts inbound Payala events on a TCP listener and client-asserted offline batches via POST /sync/payala; it has no outbound Payala API client."
impala-card/README.md:6-7 → see next gap.

gaps.title: No threat-model document; CONTRIBUTING.md points at one that does not exist
gaps.detail: CONTRIBUTING.md:44-45 says the threat model lives in impala-bridge/SECURITY.md; that file enumerates controls but no assets, trust boundaries or adversaries. Card and contract threats are not modelled anywhere.
gaps.suggested_approach: Add docs/threat-model.md with this outline. 1 Assets: card-local balance (myBalance); card P-256 private key; SCP03 static keys; user/master PINs; bridge JWT_SECRET and auth epochs; custodial managed_seed rows (reserve seed generate-only); reserve pool funds (XLM/USDC/USDT0/USD float); wrapper-contract USDC and signer set; provider credentials; PII in impala_account. 2 Trust boundaries: card ↔ terminal/phone (NFC, unauthenticated except PIN/SCP03); phone ↔ bridge (TLS, JWT/cookie); bridge ↔ Postgres/Redis (fail-closed on Redis); bridge ↔ Horizon/RPC (network-passphrase check, ambiguous submits freeze); bridge ↔ KMS/Vault (envelope, account-bound headers); bridge ↔ exchange providers (HMAC/RSA-verified webhooks); deployer ↔ contract (unauthenticated initialize). 3 Adversaries and current posture: (a) malicious terminal — can present arbitrary signables to SIGN_TRANSFER (card enforces sender/recipient/currency/amount/PIN only), can rewrite name/gender, can INITIALIZE an unissued card; cannot extract the key; mitigation gaps: no transaction display, no terminal authentication. (b) cloned/emulated card — can sign without debiting and be accepted by any receiving card because pubKeySig is not verified and no issuer key exists; only detectable by (non-existent) reconciliation. (c) compromised bridge signer / DB writer — managed_seed address-binding assertion and account-bound header stop seed transplant; reserve seed generate-only; replenishment caps; ambiguous submits never auto-retried. (d) malicious deployer — can front-run initialize, point contract at look-alike token; mitigation: verify usdc_token()/signers off-chain before funding; __constructor deferred. (e) lagging or lying Horizon — deposit watcher commit-then-advance cursor, float guard on min(ledger, on-chain), startup passphrase check; residual: trustline audit is warn-only when Horizon unreachable. (f) insider admin — seven-role capability matrix, typed confirm phrases for key replacement, audit outbox events, 600 s reverse cooldown; residual: ADMIN_ACCOUNT_IDS break-glass bypasses granular scoping; SET_FULL_NAME unauthenticated. 4 Out of scope / accepted: shared-NAT lockout, Redis flush re-enabling tokens until TTL, no physical-card tamper claims. 5 Per-claim evidence pointer to the capability matrix.
